observations: Photo 0: white and pink domestic-style sewing machine with dial marked pattern selector, brand name partly visible as 'Riccar' near top right, watermark 'MARTEX GLOBAL'
Photo 1: different white sewing machine, box reads 'Semco indigo 6', background shows a 'SINGER' box and other machines, same watermark
Photo 2: third white sewing machine labeled 'NOVAMATIC NM 868A' with multicolor stitch-pattern panel, same watermark
All three machines have different body shapes, dial layouts, and brand markings - they are not the same unit photographed from different angles
None of the three show the classic industrial sewing-machine form (flat-bed on a stand with external motor and belt); all appear to be portable domestic/semi-industrial zigzag machines
Background in all photos shows a cluttered shop with many other sewing machines, suggesting a dealer's showroom rather than a single item being sold

identity.kind: portable domestic sewing machine (multiple different units shown)

claims.evidence: All three photos show compact, multi-stitch domestic/semi-industrial machines with plastic housings and pattern dials, not the heavy single-stitch industrial flatbed form factor

claims.claim: Used for sewing of clothes and multipurpose uses
claims.evidence: No video or test run shown of stitching in action

risks.risk: Listing shows three different machines (Riccar, Semco Indigo 6, Novamatic NM 868A) under one ad - unclear which single item is actually for sale
risks.proof: Seller must confirm and photograph the single exact unit being sold, with its nameplate and serial number in one frame
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified/unverified single item, cannot assign one unit's worth

risks.risk: Claim of 'industrial' machine not matching domestic-style photos
risks.proof: A photo of the machine's motor/base and belt-drive or stand, which industrial machines typically have
risks.if_unproven: priced as a standard portable domestic machine, not industrial-grade

risks.risk: Working condition unknown - no power-on or stitching demonstration
risks.proof: Short video of the machine running and producing a stitch line on fabric

risks.risk: Missing accessories (foot pedal, power cord, bobbins) which affect usability and price
risks.proof: Photo of all included accessories laid out together
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare machine only, no accessories included

proof_requests: Clear photo of the single machine actually being sold, including its full nameplate/serial number
Video of the machine powered on and stitching a sample piece of fabric
Photo showing the motor/base assembly to confirm industrial vs domestic build
Photo of all accessories included (pedal, cord, bobbins, extra feet)
response.reason: The ad for a single 'industrial sewing machine' shows three distinctly different branded machines (Riccar, Semco Indigo 6, Novamatic NM 868A), none of which match the industrial description, indicating either a mismatched/stock-photo listing or an attempt to pass off multiple unrelated units as one item.
